coding_scope.blinding: Partial. Participant labels were treated as opaque IDs; no arm map or policy text was read. Role/model and intervention clues are inferable from the locked decision language, so this is not guaranteed arm-blind coding.
coding_scope.source_boundary: The scenario source-unit map was used. Individual source snapshots were not needed and were not read. No project execution, test, build, external research, or code change was performed.
coding_scope.counting_note: One assignment can carry multiple independently discriminable questions; one question can recur across assignments/phases. Assignment and conversation counts are not question counts. Registration or planned coverage is not execution or achieved coverage.

question_catalog.purpose: Determine whether a rejected store update changes the intended record state.
question_catalog.discriminator: Matched valid/rejected update on the same identified executable, inputs and configuration, comparing complete before/after snapshots with record IDs.
question_catalog.qualification: Directly addresses the report and separates actual mutation from missing IDs, rebuild or mismatched artifact.
question_catalog.ambiguity: The CLI and store concerns share assignments in both plans but are separate mechanisms; count this as one store question.

question_catalog.purpose: Determine whether a CLI batch emits an earlier valid row before rejecting a later invalid value.
question_catalog.discriminator: Matched valid-only and valid-then-invalid batches; capture stdout, stderr and status under the same invocation/configuration.
question_catalog.qualification: The output timing/validation contract is independently observable and decision-relevant.
question_catalog.ambiguity: Split from Q01 and Q03 although p29 P01 and p61 A1 group them with other checks.

question_catalog.purpose: Determine whether redirected --help failure follows the output sink or CLI behavior.
question_catalog.discriminator: Compare --help to a normal file and a failing sink such as system-fixture/dev/full where available; capture status/output.
question_catalog.qualification: Separately discriminable from batch output and explicitly bounded by sink availability.
question_catalog.ambiguity: The planned test mentions system-fixture/dev/full only where available; unsupported sink is setup-limited, not a failed hypothesis.

question_catalog.purpose: Identify the actual configured and linked text provider/package, then compare the same non-ASCII bytes through the real C++ caller.
question_catalog.discriminator: Provider/package/library marker and artifact identity plus matched bytes, valid control and caller path.
question_catalog.qualification: Separates package/provider identity and caller behavior; a test pass without linked-provider identity is inconclusive.
question_catalog.ambiguity: R09 is relevant to selected package/path evidence, not an automatic standalone question.

question_catalog.purpose: Find the first divergence from equivalent adapter events through normalization, shared application state and presentation.
question_catalog.discriminator: Same edit/submit sequence and snapshots across affected/reference adapters, recording normalized events, authoritative records/status and rendered view.
question_catalog.qualification: Matches the specified GUI symptom and traces a decision-relevant cross-layer boundary.
question_catalog.ambiguity: R04 was already investigated initially. E2 adds the direct-versus-installed-consumer comparison in Q12; it does not create a second generic GUI question.

question_catalog.purpose: Determine whether progress after cancel/restart is produced by a stale generation or displayed incorrectly.
question_catalog.discriminator: Capture generation at production, mailbox and application consumption in a gated start/cancel/start sequence; compare with the native task fixture.
question_catalog.qualification: Independent lifecycle mechanism and a feasible focused fixture with an explicit scheduling limit.
question_catalog.ambiguity: Grouped with R04 in p29 P03; source path and discriminator make this independently countable.

question_catalog.purpose: Determine whether a transient send failure prevents polling rescheduling or whether client/transport/view state blocks refresh.
question_catalog.discriminator: Matched success, rejection and recovery with same scheduler/client; capture timers, sends, lifecycle flags and view update, then trace the identified browser transport.
question_catalog.qualification: Separates polling lifecycle from downstream transport and presentation, with fixture limits stated.
question_catalog.ambiguity: Does not establish behavior in every browser.

question_catalog.purpose: Determine which nested view consumes wheel input and whether overflow/focus changes the result; trace retained-input consumer only as needed.
question_catalog.discriminator: Same wheel event on fitting versus overflowing/clamped read-only child; record child/parent offsets, focus and selection, and selected input path.
question_catalog.qualification: Tests the stated child/ancestor interaction boundary; R11 grounds a consumer path rather than adding a question by itself.
question_catalog.ambiguity: The patch/input identity and retained-kernel constraints limit scope; no kernel configuration is proposed.

question_catalog.purpose: Determine whether editor displacement originates in changed model data or the canvas transform/render path.
question_catalog.discriminator: Hold project point, viewport, pan and zoom; compare model-to-view/view-to-model round trip, bounds and paint/hit results before/after value change.
question_catalog.qualification: A bounded, matched geometry check directly separates two plausible layers.
question_catalog.ambiguity: R08 shares an assignment with the flow report; it is a separate mechanism.

question_catalog.purpose: Determine where a completed editor flow loses items between production and downstream consumption.
question_catalog.discriminator: Same graph/data and mode; compare produced/consumed counts, exact sink sequence and terminal state.
question_catalog.qualification: Separates producer, edge and consumer truncation and names a focused fixture.
question_catalog.ambiguity: The flow fixture samples modes and does not establish all consumers.

question_catalog.purpose: Establish which build or retained-input consumer, test registrations, prerequisites and wrapper limits materially constrain the eight planned discriminators.
question_catalog.discriminator: Check selected source/group/manifest against actual consumer, relevant registered targets, and only those path/process/capacity helper contracts that planned checks depend on.
question_catalog.qualification: A focused feasibility question prevents setup failures being misread as regressions and covers the planned build/retained-input consumer layer.
question_catalog.ambiguity: Broad but conditionally scoped to constraints on the proposed discriminators. The source units do not imply all are implicated. p61 has R11 in Q08 but no matching R09-R12 feasibility assignment; do not count incidental references as this question.

question_catalog.purpose: For the new direct-pass/installed-stale-view observation, find the first divergence for the same valid edit/submit across direct and installed consumers.
question_catalog.discriminator: Trace event normalization, shared records/status, provider/transport boundary and presentation snapshots in both consumers; retain competing layers until matched traces identify divergence.
question_catalog.qualification: E2 supplies a new consumer comparison absent from the original report; concrete, bounded and decision-relevant. Astra's request for the smallest matched boundary discriminator duplicates this Luna-owned question and is counted as co-participation, not another question.
question_catalog.ambiguity: E2 also changes prioritization and refines Q05. Count one added question because the installed-vs-direct comparison is a new discriminator, not because assignment P03/A2 was rerouted.

question_catalog.purpose: Establish what matching declared manifest/source revision does and does not show, and identify installed artifact, selected/linked provider and test-inventory differences.
question_catalog.discriminator: Compare declared source/manifest with actual runtime binary/library/provider marker, package identity and executed test list for the named consumers.
question_catalog.qualification: This is a separate identity/configuration question needed to interpret the new consumer report; it is not a cause claim and cannot substitute for Q12's matched behavioral trace.
question_catalog.ambiguity: R09/ R11 are source-map coverage for package/consumer paths. In p61 the request appears in combined R01/R03 and R04 follow-up work; these records add no independent assignment or model slot.

source_coverage_planned_by_question.both_E1: No question-scope expansion; retain initial coverage.
source_coverage_planned_by_question.both_E2: No new distinct source unit beyond those already planned; add consumer-specific comparisons within R03/R04/R09/R11.

rejected_or_non_incremental.coordination_screening_review_execution_: Excluded as new factual questions unless they state a novel discriminator: Terra ledger/request/screen assignments; Sol decision and patch review gates; generic conditional test execution and repair assignments. They remain valid process/quality obligations, not question counts.
rejected_or_non_incremental.E2_duplicate_advisory: Astra's matched-boundary recommendation is co-participation in Q12, not a separate Q14.
rejected_or_non_incremental.other_source_units: A source unit mentioned by a broad screen, reviewer or neighboring caller is not itself a new investigation question.

same_question_routing: Q05/Q12 remain Luna factual investigation in both planners. E2's direct-versus-installed discriminator is added under the existing R04 assignment; Astra supplies strategic advice on the same discriminator. No question moved from Sol/Astra to Luna or Terra.
Q04 remains Luna across phases; E1 sharpens provider/package identity after an unmarked success. That is continuation of its original question, not new work.
Q01 remains Luna across phases; E1 adds same-artifact/ID controls after an uncontrolled rebuilt-binary report. That is continuation, not a new question.
Q09 and Q10 are separate investigations grouped under the same R08 assignment. Q02 and Q03 are separate CLI questions grouped with store under p29 P01 and with store/provider under p61 A1.

P29 P03 and p61 A2 are marked reroute at E2 but retain Luna, role and conversation identity. The scope/priority changes to the E2 consumer branch; the data does not show a model/owner transfer. Treat the action label as a routing-status ambiguity, not evidence of a new worker or slot.

E_event_response.E1: Both planners preserve the original R01/R03 uncertainty, ask for missing artifact/input/provider details, and keep independent report work moving. No E1 feedback becomes a controlled reproduction or provider-specific pass; no new discriminating investigation question is introduced.
E_event_response.E2: Both planners prioritize a new direct-versus-installed R04 trace and runtime/provider/test-inventory identity checks while retaining R01/R03 controls and the other report work. p29 activates Astra; p61 activates Astra in parallel with the Luna trace. Neither treats the invented report as their own experiment or as a root cause. Human requests seek consumer artifact, test list, provider, event, timing and state/presentation evidence; no human response is represented in the locked files.

acceptance_limits: Useful means planned source-grounded, decision-relevant, feasible and nonredundant candidate work; no accepted finding or project outcome is established.
Counts are coding judgments from the specified six locked records only; they do not show work executed, test coverage achieved, actual model dispatches, costs or savings.
The p29/p61 labels may be inferable from decision language; arm-blindness is partial and no target number of questions was assumed.
